name: Global Bitcoin Circular Economies Summit 2026
description:
## Bitcoin Circular Economies Summit 2026 Two years ago, the Bitcoin Circular Economies Summit was a closed room. Leaders from circular economies around the world, comparing notes, figuring out together what actually works when you try to make Bitcoin a daily medium of exchange instead of a speculative bet. Quiet work. The kind nobody tweets about while it's happening. ‍On November 19-20, 2026, the Global Bitcoin Circular Economies Summit becomes a public conference for the first time, and it's happening in El Zonte. Not San Salvador. Not a hotel ballroom somewhere convenient. El Zonte, the same stretch of sand where this whole story started, where people were paying for pupusas and surfboards in sats years before anyone outside the country had heard of Bitcoin Beach. ‍It's the first conference of its kind this town has ever hosted. And there's really only one thing it could be about: Bitcoin is money, and the circular economies are the proof

‍Two Years of Building Toward This ‍For two Summits, the focus was internal. Builders talking to builders. Communities in El Salvador, Africa, Southeast Asia, Latin America, comparing what worked, what failed, what scaled. It turned into a real global conversation, even if most people never saw it happen. ‍The 2026 edition finally opens that conversation to everyone who's been curious from the outside. Leaders, merchants, educators, developers, and honestly, anyone who wants to see what Bitcoin adoption looks like when it's not a headline but a Tuesday afternoon at a market stall

‍What Two Days Actually Look Like ‍This isn't a stage with slides and a Q&A at the end. It's workshops, panels, and fireside chats built around the questions that actually define where Bitcoin adoption goes next: ‍● Bitcoin is money: the case from on-the-ground reality● Circular economies: what's working, what's scaling, what's next● Bitcoin for merchants: practical adoption at the point of sale● Education: onboarding the next million users● Adoption: pathways from curiosity to daily use● Tools: the infrastructure powering real-world Bitcoin commerce ‍Every session wraps before sunset. This is El Zonte, after all, and nobody organizing this event forgot that the ocean is right there

‍Who's Already Confirmed ‍The lineup is still growing, but a few names are already locked in, and they set the tone for what this Summit is actually about: ‍● Jeremy Almond (@jeremyalmond), Co-Founder & CEO of Paystand● Alexandra Navarro (@alex_navarro0), also from Paystand● Gerardo Linares (@GR_Linares1), driving Bitcoin adoption through education and real-world circular economies with Bitcoin Berlin SV and Bitcoin La Laguna● Evelyn Lemus (@Evelynlemus2906), building and educating communities through the same two projects ‍Not a single one of them is on this list because of a headline they made. They're here because they took Bitcoin out of theory and put it directly into the hands of people who never had financial access before. That's the thread running through this whole event

‍A Beach, Not a Backdrop ‍Come for the panels, but stay for the reason this movement exists in the first place. You're going to hear it straight from the people who built it: why Bitcoin is money, why it matters for the people who've been failed by every other financial system, and why freedom and fairness aren't abstract words when you've watched them play out in a small coastal town. ‍And between sessions, there's still surf if you want it, there's still that particular warmth of Bitcoin Country that doesn't translate to a conference center anywhere else. This isn't a Bitcoin summit that happens to be near a beach. It only makes sense on this one

‍November in El Salvador Is Getting Busy ‍This isn't even the only Bitcoin event on the calendar this month, and that alone says something about where this country is right now: ‍● November 10 — Bitcoin Capital Summit● November 11-12 — Bitcoin Historico, San Salvador● November 18-19 — EmTech AI Conference● November 19-20 — Global Bitcoin Circular Economies Summit, El Zonte ‍Four events, one month, in a country that used to make headlines for very different reasons. Now it's builders, educators, and investors filling flights to come see what's actually being built here

‍We're Genuinely Looking Forward to This One ‍Every year this Summit has been a working session behind closed doors. This year, for the first time, everyone gets to be in the room, and that shift feels like a real milestone, not just for the event but for the movement it represents. El Zonte earned this. The people who built circular economies from nothing, in El Salvador and around the world, earned a stage. ‍Seats are limited, and this is the first time El Zonte has hosted anything like it. If you want to hear, in their own words, why Bitcoin is money, this is the place to be

Every SAT count

Today he is founder and CEO of Next Decentrum and editor of The Streetlight on Substack. Mike Nabavi, six-time founder. His payments venture LavaPay had a pipeline nearing $9M a month when its banks shut it down, which led to Omnieon, infrastructure for federated finance. Today he works as an interim or fractional executive for early-stage and owner-operated companies. Ask Mike anything, including what he got wrong. description: **Die 7. Females Fit for Finance-Edition hosted by Sara Bratke & Marika Cieslinski** **Thema**: Lerne mit Margot Richter über die Kryptowährung „Bitcoin“ und wie du zu deiner finanziellen Souveränität beitragen kannst **Über das Event** Die Möglichkeiten zu investieren und einen Wertspeicher zu finden, sind heute vielfältig und die Flut an Informationen kann schnell überfordern. Aktien, ETFs, Gold, Immobilien und dann gibt es da auch noch Kryptowährungen wie Bitcoin. Margot Richter zeigt, warum Bitcoin für sie ein spannendes Werkzeug ist, um sich als Frau mit finanzieller Unabhängigkeit, Inflation, Altersvorsorge und langfristigem Werterhalt auseinanderzusetzen. Das Event ist kostenlos (wir freuen uns über freiwillige Spenden). **Inhalt des Impuls-Vortrags** Bevor wir uns Bitcoin genauer ansehen, lohnt sich ein Blick auf etwas, das wir täglich verwenden, aber selten hinterfragen: unser Geldsystem. Margot gibt eine kurze Einführung, wie unser heutiges Geld eigentlich funktioniert, wer es beeinflusst und was das für den Wert unseres Geldes in Zukunft bedeutet. Darauf aufbauend führt Margot verständlich in die Welt von Bitcoin ein. Sie erklärt, was Bitcoin ist, was Bitcoin zum souveränen Wertspeicher machen kann und welche Vorteile und Möglichkeiten Bitcoin gegenüber anderen Investments bietet. Der Vortrag richtet sich an Frauen, die bisher wenig oder gar keine Berührung mit Bitcoin hatten und das Thema besser verstehen möchten. **Über Margot Richter** Margot beschäftigt sich seit 2020 intensiv mit Bitcoin, Finanz-und Wirtschaftsthemen. Sie gibt hierzu Einsteigerkurse via der Bildungsplatform "Bitucation", organisiert Bitcoin Veranstaltungen für Frauen und ist in der deutschsprachigen Bitcoin Community sehr engagiert. Sie gründete außerdem den "Bitcoin Book Club". Als ausgebildete Wanderinstruktorin leitet sie ebenfalls Wanderungen in Österreich. Margot arbeitet als selbstständige Physiotherapeutin in Wien. Bitfest is the UK’s flagship Bitcoin festival. The 2026 edition is a four-day Bitcoin festival in Manchester, taking place from 19–22 November 2026. It brings together Bitcoiners, builders, communities, artists, families and newcomers for talks, workshops, an expo, art, cinema, gaming, live music, Nostr and freedom technology. So… is it a conference? Well, yes and no. Bitfest is a space where people from all walks of life can come together for a weekend powered by Bitcoiners. It’s about community as much as it is about technology: a place to connect, learn, explore, and actually experience Bitcoin culture in action. While talks and panels are part of the programme, Bitfest goes far beyond a traditional conference – incorporating talks, discussions and hands-on workshops covering not just Bitcoin, but other freedom-adjacent topics. Our inaugural event, Bitfest 2025, featured 5 events and 8 themed zones across 3 days, with 60+ speakers and artists, all hosted across multiple nearby venues. And now Bitfest is back for 2026. Bigger, louder and with even more to explore! This year’s programme brings together a staggering 8 events and 9 zones, creating an even bigger celebration of Bitcoin, freedom technology, creativity and the communities building the future. Bitfest is designed for everyone – whether you’re deep in the space or just getting started. It’s family-friendly too and so bring the kids along! Bitfest is the UK’s flagship Bitcoin festival, bringing together Bitcoin, Nostr, freedom technology, music, art, culture, workshops, gaming, businesses and communities for one packed long weekend in Manchester. When is Bitfest 2026? Bitfest 2026 runs from 19–22 November 2026, with different events taking place across the long weekend. Where is Bitfest? Bitfest’s main venue is The Pendulum Hotel in Manchester, with events taking place at nearby venues throughout the weekend. Do I need to know about Bitcoin to attend? Absolutely not. Bitfest is for everyone — from people who have been running nodes for years to people who have only just heard about Bitcoin. Come curious, ask questions and get involved. How do I get to Bitfest? Driving From the North — M6 / M61 Follow the M6/M61 towards Manchester, then join the M60 following signs for Stretford. Take M60 Junction 12 and join the M602 towards Salford/Manchester. At the end of the M602, follow the A57 towards Manchester. Continue onto the A57(M) Mancunian Way and take the second exit, then immediately follow the slip road signed University/Sackville Street. The Pendulum is on Sackville Street. From the South & Midlands — M6 Follow the M6 north and leave at Junction 19, taking the A556 towards Manchester. At the Bowdon roundabout, take the third exit onto the M56 towards Manchester Airport/Manchester. Continue to the end of the M56 and follow the A5103 towards Manchester. At the roundabout beneath the road, take the third exit following A57(M) / Sheffield signs, then take the second exit up the ramp onto the A57(M). Take the next exit signed University and immediately fork left onto the slip road for University/Sackville Street. The Pendulum is ahead on Sackville Street. From London — M40 / M42 / M6 Follow the M40 north, then the M42/M6 towards Manchester. Continue on the M6 north and leave at Junction 19, then follow the South & Midlands directions above via the A556 and M56. From Manchester Airport — M56 Take the M56 towards Manchester. At the end of the motorway, continue onto the A5103 towards Manchester and follow the same route as above: take the third exit at the roundabout following A57(M) / Sheffield, then the second exit onto the A57(M). Take the next exit signed University and follow the slip road for University/Sackville Street. Public Transport From Manchester Piccadilly: The Pendulum is around a 10–15 minute walk from Manchester Piccadilly station, or a short taxi ride. From Manchester Oxford Road: The Pendulum is only a few minutes’ walk from Manchester Oxford Road station. From Manchester Airport: Direct trains run from Manchester Airport to Manchester Piccadilly, normally taking around 20 minutes. From Piccadilly, The Pendulum is a short walk or taxi ride. Manchester is also well connected by rail from cities across the UK, including London, Birmingham, Leeds, Liverpool and Sheffield. Is there parking nearby? Yes. There are several car parks within walking distance of The Pendulum, including NCP Circle Square on Oxford Road, which is just a couple of minutes from the hotel. We’ll add further details, including any Bitfest/Pendulum parking discounts or codes, here once confirmed. What does my ticket include? There are several ticket options depending on how much of the festival you want to experience. A Full Bitfest Ticket gives you access across the main festival programme and includes the exclusive Bitflix Pre-Event Reception. Can I buy a One Day Pass? Yes. A One Day Pass can be used for Nostrshire on 20 November or Bitfest on 21 November, and includes access to all zones and the relevant afterparty. What is Bitflix? Bitflix is our Bitcoin Film Zone, returning this year as a pre-festival event. It kicks off the festival with a screening of The Six Billion Dollar Man, followed by the Bitflix Pre-Event Reception. It’s a chance to start the weekend with a great film, good conversation and the wider Bitfest community. Who can attend the Bitflix Pre-Event Reception? The Pre-Event Reception is an exclusive benefit for Full Bitfest Ticket holders. One Day Pass and Afterparty-only tickets do not include access to the reception. Are children welcome at Bitfest? Yes. Bitfest is family-friendly, and children are welcome. For ticketing purposes, a child is anyone under 16. Can I leave my children in the Kids Zone? Yes. The Kids Zone is a supervised play space for children during the festival where they can play safely while parents enjoy the event. It is not intended as a formal childcare or day-care service. The team are DBS checked and appropriate safeguarding procedures are in place. Where can I see the full agenda? The full agenda, including timings, speakers, workshops, performances and other programme details, will be published separately as we get closer to the festival. Can I pay for my ticket with Bitcoin? Yes. Bitfest tickets are available to purchase in Bitcoin or fiat. I've never been to a Bitcoin event before. Will I fit in? Definitely. Bitfest is deliberately broader than a traditional Bitcoin conference. Whether you’re a hardcore Bitcoiner, a Nostr user, a builder, artist, musician, entrepreneur, parent or simply curious about what all the fuss is about, you’re welcome. Book at the Bitfest rate using code BITFEST — Book now. If the Pendulum is full, there are several other hotels within a few minutes’ walk of the venue.
